chunks.title: Purchase and sales order workflows
chunks.heading: Purchase and sales order workflows
chunks.content: Orders use guided lifecycle states so stock, commitments, credits, and accounting documents stay aligned. Use the action offered on the order rather than manually recreating stock or financial effects elsewhere.

chunks.title: Purchase and sales order workflows
chunks.heading: Partial customer fulfilment
chunks.content: A customer sales order can be fulfilled incrementally. Shipping part of an order leaves the remaining quantity committed on the original order. Each fulfilment reduces stock and commitments only by the shipped quantity. The final fulfilment completes the order.

chunks.title: Purchase and sales order workflows
chunks.heading: Resolving an outstanding balance
chunks.content: For a partially fulfilled sales order, Resolve Outstanding can leave the balance open, cancel it, or transfer it to a held child order. This avoids repeating stock movements already recorded by the original shipment.

chunks.title: Purchase and sales order workflows
chunks.heading: Partial supplier receipts
chunks.content: A purchase order can be received incrementally. Record only quantities actually received. Remaining quantities stay outstanding until a later receipt or an approved resolution path is used.

chunks.title: Purchase and sales order workflows
chunks.heading: Why some direct edits are unavailable
chunks.content: Actions may be restricted after stock, payments, credits, or external accounting documents exist. These restrictions preserve the audit trail. Use the order's amendment, resolution, credit, or reversal workflow where available.

chunks.title: POS register and selling workflows
chunks.heading: POS register and selling workflows
chunks.content: The POS supports product search, barcode scanning, parked sales, split payments, receipts, returns, register sessions, and end-of-day reconciliation. Available controls depend on the signed-in operator and location.

chunks.title: POS register and selling workflows
chunks.heading: Location and register access
chunks.content: POS users work within their assigned location and active register. Stock and register information shown by the assistant is limited to that verified context. A manager may be required for protected adjustments.

chunks.title: POS register and selling workflows
chunks.heading: Working offline
chunks.content: The POS can continue supported selling workflows while offline using its local product cache and queue. AI assistance requires a network connection and does not queue requests for later processing.

chunks.title: POS register and selling workflows
chunks.heading: Returns and store credit
chunks.content: Returns use the linked credit-note workflow so stock and customer credit are recorded once. Store credit is ledger-owned and should not be manually overwritten through customer contact editing.

chunks.title: Finding your way around Solvantis
chunks.heading: Finding your way around Solvantis
chunks.content: Solvantis shows tools according to the signed-in user's role and the part of the platform they are using. If a screen or action is unavailable, check that the user is signed in to the correct workspace and has the required access before changing the workflow.

chunks.title: Finding your way around Solvantis
chunks.heading: Getting help for the current screen
chunks.content: Ask about the outcome you need, including the order, product, location, or account involved when appropriate. Solvantis can explain the supported workflow and, where permission allows, inspect current read-only business information. It will not make changes on your behalf.

chunks.title: Finding your way around Solvantis
chunks.heading: When a workflow differs
chunks.content: Some outcomes have a specific supported path to protect stock, financial records, or account ownership. A different sequence is not necessarily an error. Solvantis should explain the supported alternative and confirm whether it meets the essential business requirement.

chunks.title: Wholesale ordering and account access
chunks.heading: Wholesale ordering and account access
chunks.content: The wholesale portal shows the approved catalogue, pricing, availability, account details, saved lists, drafts, and orders available to the signed-in company member and assigned buying location.

chunks.title: Wholesale ordering and account access
chunks.heading: Catalogue and pricing
chunks.content: Catalogue results use current product availability, approved brand access, wholesale pricing, stock, and indent policy. Historical order prices do not replace current catalogue pricing when reordering.

chunks.title: Wholesale ordering and account access
chunks.heading: Drafts and submitted orders
chunks.content: Drafts remain editable until submitted. Submitted sales orders are read-only in the buyer portal and show buyer-safe lifecycle, product, fulfilment, terms, and total information. Internal supplier notes are never shown.

chunks.title: Wholesale ordering and account access
chunks.heading: Account and location boundaries
chunks.content: Orders and drafts are restricted to the active contact, company, member, and buying-location identity. A member cannot inspect another company's orders or switch location unless that capability is explicitly supported for the account.

chunks.title: Wholesale ordering and account access
chunks.heading: Reordering
chunks.content: Reordering rebuilds a cart using current catalogue data. Retired or unavailable lines may be omitted, stock-limited lines may be reduced, and current pricing and indent rules always apply.
